finding.quote: : `reviewed head: ${facts.head}${headInput === undefined ? "" : " (given by the agent, replaces the recorded head)"}`,
finding.problem: The review_complete card accepts a model-supplied head (7-40 hex) that managed.ts uses to replace manifest.target.head before completeHeadGate. The card shows the agent value, not the recorded head, and the digest does not cover the difference.
finding.impact: Attack vector: an agent (or an injected instruction in the reviewed PR) calls review_complete with head set to the PR's current head SHA after the PR moved past the commit the round actually reviewed. The head gate passes, the manifest records the agent's SHA, and the operator is asked to approve a card whose SHA looks like the current head. The round closes as if it reviewed the latest commit. The brief requires card content (SHA) to come from the package, not from model input; the CLI `--head` is typed by the operator, the card path is typed by the model. Mitigations that keep this from being a blocker: the card does label the value as agent-given, the operator must still press yes, and the gate still demands READY and an evidence level.
finding.suggested_fix: Preferred: drop `head` from the review_complete input schema and from buildCard/apply, so the card always completes against the head the package recorded; an operator who really needs a different head uses `keryx review complete --head` in a terminal. Alternative: keep the field but show the recorded head next to it on the card (`recorded head: <sha>; the agent asks to replace it with <sha>`), refuse a value that does not prefix-match the recorded head, and fold the recorded head into factsDigest.
finding.evidence: src/commands/operator-confirm-review.ts:703 declares `head` in the tool input; :679 `head: headInput ?? recorded`; :725 renders the agent value without the recorded one; :753 `...(headInput === undefined ? {} : { head: headInput })` is passed to completeReviewGated. src/review/managed.ts:967-979 replaces `manifest.target.head` with the supplied value and only pushes a warning when it differs from the recorded head; :982 runs completeHeadGate on the replaced manifest. The CLI reaches the same code with an operator-typed --head (src/commands/review.ts runComplete -> completeReviewGated).

finding.quote: export async function answerChunkEstimate(packageDir: string, value: "yes" | "no", quote: string, now: Date = new Date(), confirmedVia?: ConfirmedVia, press?: CardPress): Promise<ChunkEstimateRecord> {
finding.problem: press?: CardPress was added as a sixth positional parameter of answerChunkEstimate (and a fifth of recordCoverageWaiver); a trailing optional positional parameter on a long signature should be an options object.
finding.impact: The card caller already holds one object that carries all of it (`confirmation`: quote, at, confirmedVia, pressedBy, pressedAt) and takes it apart again at the call: `answerChunkEstimate(prepared.dir, prepared.answer, confirmation.quote, new Date(confirmation.at), confirmation.confirmedVia, cardPressFields(confirmation))` (src/commands/operator-confirm-review.ts:157) and the same for recordCoverageWaiver (operator-confirm-review.ts:294). The next field the confirmation gains is a seventh parameter. The terminal caller src/commands/review-chunks.ts:142 passes three and relies on the defaults, so it does not share the cost. waiveReadiness and recordPlanConfirmation in the same PR already take an options object and are the better pattern.
finding.suggested_fix: Give both functions one trailing options/confirmation object, e.g. `confirmation?: { at?: Date; confirmedVia?: ConfirmedVia } & CardPress`, so the card call becomes `answerChunkEstimate(dir, value, quote, confirmation)` and cardPressFields is applied once inside. Keep the existing terminal call shape working by leaving the object optional.
finding.evidence: diff of src/review/chunks-estimate.ts (answerChunkEstimate signature, +/-) and src/review/coverage-complete.ts (recordCoverageWaiver signature); callers read at src/commands/operator-confirm-review.ts:157 and :294 and src/commands/review-chunks.ts:142.

finding.quote: export function cardPressFields(source: CardPress | undefined): CardPress {
finding.problem: The rule 'pressedBy/pressedAt exist only with confirmedVia remote-card' is enforced in one caller (operatorConfirmTool). cardPressFields and the eight recorders spread whatever press they receive next to any confirmedVia; the harness context carries loose optionals.
finding.impact: Defence in depth only. A future caller (or a hand-edited package) can write pressedBy with tui-card or a missing confirmedVia, and readers cannot tell the record was not pressed remotely. No present code path does it.
finding.suggested_fix: Give the record writers one helper that takes confirmedVia and the press together and drops the press unless confirmedVia is remote-card, and use it in the seven libraries and in the coverage-complete normaliser.
finding.evidence: types.ts cardPressFields reads only source.pressedBy and source.pressedAt. In coverage-complete.ts the normaliser does `...cardPressFields({ pressedBy, pressedAt })` regardless of `via`. The only gate is upstream: operator-confirm-tools.ts invoke sets the press only when the answer came from the remote card, after the allowed-id and 1-hour checks. Callers in operator-confirm-review.ts pass cardPressFields(confirmation) and so inherit that gate. No caller today passes a press with tui-card. Also reported by: review-security-code-w3:F-002, review-architecture-w2:F-003, review-architecture-w3:F-004.

finding.problem: CardPress/cardPressFields were introduced as the single shape for the press pair but pressedBy/pressedAt are re-declared and conditionally spread by hand in estimate.ts, learning/decisions.ts, write-land.ts, confirm-token.ts, operator-confirm-other.ts, flow/service.ts and interactive-tools.ts. operator-decisions.ts also spreads the pair twice (dead duplicate).
finding.impact: The invariant 'recorded only for confirmedVia remote-card' is enforced in one place (operatorConfirmTool, commands/operator-confirm-tools.ts:222-228) and the record shape is then free to drift per writer: a rename or a third field (for example a chat id) must be made in six or more files, and the cast in plan-confirmation.ts hides a divergence the compiler would otherwise report. In learning/decisions.ts and write-land.ts use the shared type and `cardPressFields` instead of the hand-written optional pairs.

finding.quote: const token = left > 0 ? `${age(left)} left of the 1-hour token` : "token expired, ask again";
finding.problem: The log's waiting() ignores expiry, and the pending line prints 'token expired, ask again' after 60 minutes for every card, though the 1-hour TTL is enforced only for remote-card answers (a tui-card can still be answered). The countdown is computed only at repaint. docs/commands-by-task.md:153 claims a time left of the token for every pending card, including undelivered ones.
finding.impact: AC6 'time left of the 1-hour token' is accurate only at the instant of opening; after expiry the surfaces keep signalling a Telegram-answerable card and tell the operator to ask again instead of answering in the shell.
finding.suggested_fix: Make waiting() take `now` and exclude entries past REMOTE_CARD_TTL_MS (or treat them as unmirrored); for an expired but still-open card print 'Telegram token expired, answer in the shell'. If live ages matter, add a coarse interval that calls the modal repaint while a card is waiting.
finding.evidence: operator-confirmations.ts waiting() has no time argument; pendingConfirmationLine branches on `left > 0`; operator-confirm-tools.ts lines 207-221 apply the TTL only on the remote path; decisions-surface.ts openDecisions calls `confirmationLines?.()` once. finding.quote: for (const old of answered.slice(0, Math.max(0, answered.length - ANSWERED_CARDS_KEPT))) {
finding.problem: Answered cards are evicted and displayed in ask order, not answer order, although entries() says newest first; a long-waiting card answered late can be evicted ahead of a quicker one.
finding.impact: The line the card exists for ('pressed by Telegram user N') can vanish the moment it is written, when approvals overlap (workers, queued cards). The answered list is not 'recent first' as documented. Sequential single-card use is unaffected, which is all the test covers.
finding.suggested_fix: Order and evict by answered.at: sort answered by `answered.at` descending in entries(), and evict the entries with the smallest `answered.at`. Add a test: ask A, ask 5 more and answer them, answer A last; expect A still present and first.
finding.evidence: operator-confirmations.ts answer(): `const answered = this.items.filter((item) => item.answered !== undefined)` then slice(0, len-5) of that insertion-ordered array; entries(): `this.items.filter(...answered !== undefined).reverse()`. Trace for A + b1..b5: answer(A) makes 6 answered, slice(0,1) = [A], spliced out. Also reported by: review-highload-w4:F-003.

finding.problem: The list of the five Telegram-answerable review cards is hand-written in four user-facing strings (help-groups.ts, agent-commands.ts descriptions) of 330-560 characters each; no single source.
finding.impact: Low. Adding a sixth remote-answerable card means editing five places; a missed one leaves help text that names the wrong set.
finding.suggested_fix: Build the parenthesised list from one exported constant of the remote-answerable card names, or add a small test that every `review_*` name in those strings is in the registry.
finding.evidence: `keryx ctx rg -n --all 'review_confirm_plan, review_decide_premise' src` (non-test): src/standard/help-groups.ts:582 and :600, src/commands/agent-commands.ts:187 and :304. Also reported by: review-clean-code-w2:F-008, review-style-w2:F-008, review-style-w3:F-004.

finding.problem: projectRemoteRow returns early on waiting cards ahead of the flow-397 branch, so a row with a card and an unconfirmed approval drops the 'N unconfirmed' note, and the card count is truncated first on the 30-column sidebar for long topic names.
finding.impact: Low: the /remote-control status tab still prints 'Approvals not confirmed: N'. Noted because the row is the only always-visible surface and its width budget is 26 columns.
finding.suggested_fix: Compose both fragments (`${topic} · ${cards} · ${unconfirmed} unconf.`) with the existing fit(), or document that cards take precedence.
finding.evidence: remote-control-surface.ts projectRemoteRow: the `cards` branch returns before the `unconfirmed > 0` branch. Also reported by: review-logic-w4:F-005.

finding.problem: The topic-only path for a Telegram-started turn (requestApprovalForTelegramTurn) never calls operatorCards.ask/answer and has no undelivered fallback; isCard also covers schedule_* cards.
finding.impact: A review_complete or confirm-plan card raised during a Telegram-started turn, which is the main case where a remote-card answer with pressedBy is recorded, is absent from the sidebar count, the status tab and the /decisions list. The 'who pressed' view is blind exactly to the cards answered remotely from a Telegram turn. Display only; the durable record is written by the gate.
finding.suggested_fix: Put the ask/answer bookkeeping at one seam both wrappers share (a small `trackOperatorCard(meta, run)` helper in operator-confirmations.ts, or a wrapper applied to both wrappers), instead of inlining it in one branch of one closure.
finding.evidence: ctx rg for `operatorCards` in src: ask() at tui-shell.ts:6103 and :6116 only; requestApprovalForTelegramTurn spans :6028-6089 with no reference to operatorCards. Also reported by: review-logic-w4:F-006, review-security-code-w4:F-003, review-regression-w4:RG-W4-001.

finding.problem: client.askApproval edge cases: the catch around POST plus response.json() marks a lost response as undelivered (false positive), a post-POST disconnect returns deny with no undelivered flag and leaves the topic card open (false negative), RemoteBridge does not set the flag on throw, and raceApproval can accept a late topic press just before settled is set.
finding.impact: Failure mode: after a slow bridge response the operator sees 'mirror not delivered' in the TUI but may still press the Telegram card; that press finds no waiter and is dropped, so it is harmless to state (fail-closed) but the note is wrong in that window. A cosmetic mislabel, not a data-integrity issue.
finding.suggested_fix: Mark undelivered: true only when the failure is known to precede the request being accepted (not connected, non-ok response, missing id); for a thrown error after send, either omit the flag or word the note as 'delivery unconfirmed'.
finding.evidence: src/remote/client.ts lines 450-462: one catch for post(), response.ok, and json() failures, returning undelivered: true. Also reported by: review-highload-w3:F-004, review-highload-w3:F-002, review-logic-w3:F-004, review-logic-w3:F-005.

finding.problem: consumeConfirmationToken builds the SignatureConfirmation without pressedBy/pressedAt although mintConfirmationToken stores them (record gap on the flow-confirm token).
finding.impact: No attack vector; an audit-completeness gap. A reader of the signature alone sees 'remote-card-token' without who pressed it.
finding.suggested_fix: If the signature is meant to be self-contained provenance, copy pressedBy/pressedAt into the returned SignatureConfirmation (types.ts already allows them on the confirmation block). Otherwise state in TM-04 that the signature references the token and the token record holds the presser.
finding.evidence: confirm-token.ts:140 stores pressedBy; confirm-token.ts:215-236 consumeConfirmationToken returns no pressedBy/pressedAt.

finding.problem: Pre-existing: entries in the process-local pending token map are removed only by invoke or confirmationDeclined; abandoned cards are never swept (the PR adds issuedAt but no eviction).
finding.impact: One small object per abandoned card. A single operator shell asks a handful of cards a day, so growth is negligible. It is a leak only in a shell that runs for months with many abandoned cards.
finding.suggested_fix: Optional: on each `confirmation()` call, drop entries older than REMOTE_CARD_TTL_MS, using the `issuedAt` this PR already stores.
finding.evidence: src/commands/operator-confirm-tools.ts: `pending.set(token, { input: key(input), card, shown, prepared: built.prepared, issuedAt: now().getTime() })` at line 192. The 1-hour TTL is checked only inside invoke for remote answers, and no timer or sweep exists. The Map and its set/delete pattern pre-date this PR; the PR only adds `issuedAt`. Also reported by: review-logic-w2:F-003, review-performance-w2:F-002.

finding.problem: completionFacts reads manifest.json, report.md and research.json synchronously, twice per card plus a third time in completeReviewGated; negligible at this load.
finding.impact: Negligible. At most a single-digit-ms stall of the TUI loop on an operator action. No scaling with N and no repetition inside a loop.
finding.suggested_fix: None required. If the file ever grows large or the card is rendered on a timer, switch to fs/promises readFile; the surrounding specs already import sync fs helpers, so the sync form is consistent with the file.
finding.evidence: Diff hunk @@ 746-877 of operator-confirm-review.ts: completionFacts() is called from buildCard and from apply. It runs in the keryx shell process, so each call blocks the event loop for the length of the three reads. Frequency: once per review_complete card plus once per yes, both driven by an operator pressing a button, a few times per review round. report.md is a text report of tens to a few hundred KB; a local read is sub-millisecond to low milliseconds. evidenceLevelLine is a linear scan (src/review/evidence-level.ts:58) and loadRemoteConfig (src/remote/config.ts:172) is one small file read, once per remote press.

finding.problem: Small style items: imports dropped mid-group in operator-confirm-review.ts, prBound without is/has prefix, factsDigest as arrow const among function declarations, placeholder package: '' in test inputs, JSDoc of formatRemoteStatusLines and projectRemoteRow not updated for the new parameters, stacked ReadinessWaiver JSDoc (pre-existing).
finding.impact: Cosmetic. The block was already unsorted before this PR, so this is not a regression, but each flow adds to it and the file now has a ten-line header comment plus about 30 import lines.
finding.suggested_fix: Place the two new imports with their group (../lib/* together, ../review/* together) the next time this block is touched; no change required for this PR.
finding.evidence: slice-02.diff, operator-confirm-review.ts import block. Also reported by: review-style-w2:F-009, review-style-w2:F-010, review-style-w4:F-005, review-clean-code-w3:F-004, review-style-w3:F-005.
